title: Safe Core: Players Who Fit Every Build
markdown:
<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** A balanced build skips the projected top 20 and fills the core with players ranked roughly 25 to 75. The safest of them get their value from points, rebounds and assists, because those categories repeat week to week. Build around Markkanen, Jalen Williams, Murphy and Kawhi in the 20 to 25 USD range. Then add 10 to 20 USD players with no weak category, such as Alexander-Walker, Anunoby, Paul George, Wagner, Fox and Rollins. Fill the end of the draft with 1 to 5 USD players who also have no weak category.

## What a safe core means in our league

The balanced build skips the projected top 20 players. It puts the 11 core players between roughly rank 25 and rank 75. The ceiling is lower, but the build is much safer. In our 144-player draft, that means most of your 200 USD goes to players ranked around 25 to 75. You do not spend 60 or more USD on one star. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1793))

The safety comes from replacement. If your best player gets hurt, you can find another player around rank 30 on waivers much more easily than you can replace a top 5 player. With daily FAB waivers and 6 adds a week, a balanced team can patch an injury within days. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1809))

Every player in this article is tagged as fitting every build, with no weak category flagged. So none of them forces a punt. The real questions are what each one costs and which of his categories you can count on every week. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1793), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1382))

## Which categories are stable

Points, rebounds and assists are high-volume stats. They are the most stable from game to game. In head-to-head, players whose strengths sit in those categories are more reliable. A steady points, rebounds and assists player is worth more than one whose value comes from steals, blocks and percentages, because his production repeats more reliably. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=2229), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=456))

Players who combine categories that usually do not go together carry extra value. Examples are rebounds with assists, or assists with steals from a forward. In this pool, Jalen Williams gives big assists and steals for a forward. Franz Wagner gives points and assists as a forward. Podziemski and Hart give a guard's assists plus rebounds. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1382), [Jalen Williams](#player/604), [Franz Wagner](#player/577), [Brandin Podziemski](#player/446), [Josh Hart](#player/225))

Some players have no weak category but get their value from steals, threes, blocks or FG%. That group includes Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, McDaniels, Okongwu and Paul George. They fit any build, but their weekly output swings more. Pair them with points and assists players. Do not stack them as your core. ([09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=456), [OG Anunoby](#player/20), [Mikal Bridges](#player/63), [Jaden McDaniels](#player/370), [Onyeka Okongwu](#player/422), [Paul George](#player/189))

## How to spend by price range

Above 35 USD sit Gilgeous-Alexander, Maxey, Haliburton and Jamal Murray. All four fit any build, but they are projected top 20 players, so the balanced plan lets other managers pay for them. If one of them falls to the experts' price range late in the auction, he is still a sound buy. That range is about 34 to 38 USD for Murray, mid-to-high 30s for Haliburton and 40 to 45 USD for Maxey. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1793), [Shai Gilgeous-Alexander](#player/192), [Tyrese Maxey](#player/362), [Tyrese Haliburton](#player/215), [Jamal Murray](#player/400))

From 20 to 25 USD, buy your anchors: Markkanen, Jalen Williams, Murphy and Kawhi Leonard. Markkanen and Murphy bring points and threes. Jalen Williams brings assists. Kawhi brings points and steals, but only near 20 to 24 USD because of his knee. Stop at the top of each player's range. Experts call 29 USD too high for Williams, and above 25 USD Murphy is priced on a role that came with Murray out. ([Lauri Markkanen](#player/350), [Jalen Williams](#player/604), [Trey Murphy III](#player/398), [Kawhi Leonard](#player/331))

From 10 to 20 USD comes the middle of the core. Alexander-Walker, Irving, Herro and Bane give points, threes and FT%. Wagner and Fox give points or assists. Rollins gives assists and steals. Anunoby, Paul George and Okongwu give steals and threes. This is where the build gets most of its depth, because market costs here often sit below expert values. ([Nickeil Alexander-Walker](#player/12), [Kyrie Irving](#player/259), [Tyler Herro](#player/234), [Desmond Bane](#player/30), [Franz Wagner](#player/577), [De'Aaron Fox](#player/179), [Ryan Rollins](#player/488), [OG Anunoby](#player/20), [Paul George](#player/189), [Onyeka Okongwu](#player/422))

From 5 to 12 USD, take upside pieces: Harper for assists, LaVine and Powell for points, McDaniels for defense and FG%, and Coward as a balanced wing. For the last bench spots, use 1 to 5 USD fillers such as Podziemski, Hart, Wiggins and Mikal Bridges. If one of them disappoints, you can replace him from waivers. ([Dylan Harper](#player/222), [Zach LaVine](#player/328), [Norman Powell](#player/459), [Jaden McDaniels](#player/370), [Cedric Coward](#player/120), [Brandin Podziemski](#player/446), [Josh Hart](#player/225), [Andrew Wiggins](#player/598), [Mikal Bridges](#player/63))

## Where the sources disagree

Prices for several core players are disputed. For Murphy, Yahoo says 30 USD and ESPN says 12 USD. Josh and our past auction point to the low 20s. For Paul George, most experts see 10 to 15 USD as good value, while Josh would go up to 20 USD. For Markkanen, the experts give a round 3 grade that fits a mid-20s bid, but one mock already reached 30 USD. For Kawhi, ESPN's 40 USD value goes against the expert cap of 24 USD. For Mikal Bridges, ESPN's 26 USD value goes against an expert value of about 2 USD. In each case, our plan follows the expert range and not the higher site value. ([Trey Murphy III](#player/398), [Paul George](#player/189), [Lauri Markkanen](#player/350), [Kawhi Leonard](#player/331), [Mikal Bridges](#player/63))

## Playoff schedule and early checks

Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21 and end 2027-03-28, so schedules matter for a core you plan to hold. Dallas (Irving), Memphis (Coward) and Phoenix (Miles Bridges) play 4-4-4. Haliburton plays only 3-4-3. Minnesota (McDaniels) has a two-game semifinal week. The Knicks (Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Hart), Miami (Wiggins) and Houston (Sheppard) have weak schedules. Plan to trade Knicks and Miami players before the 2027-03-04 deadline. ([Kyrie Irving](#player/259), [Cedric Coward](#player/120), [Miles Bridges](#player/64), [Tyrese Haliburton](#player/215), [Jaden McDaniels](#player/370), [OG Anunoby](#player/20), [Mikal Bridges](#player/63), [Josh Hart](#player/225), [Andrew Wiggins](#player/598), [Reed Sheppard](#player/513))

In the first two to three weeks, check minutes and role first. Kawhi's and Irving's back-to-back games, Jalen Williams's hamstring, Wagner keeping the point guard role and Rollins keeping his starting job decide whether these players stay in your core. A balanced build can drop a player who misses these marks and replace him from waivers. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1809), [Kawhi Leonard](#player/331), [Kyrie Irving](#player/259), [Jalen Williams](#player/604), [Franz Wagner](#player/577), [Ryan Rollins](#player/488))

## Players

Prices in USD. Yahoo and ESPN: rank and average auction cost for 2026-27.

### Above 35 USD: outside the balanced core

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Shai Gilgeous-Alexander](#player/192) | OKC | G | 4 | 66.8 | 3 | 73.2 | 81 | He has no weak category and gives elite points, but as a top 4 pick he is exactly the kind of player the balanced build skips. |
| [Tyrese Maxey](#player/362) | PHI | G | 8 | 56.5 | 8 | 48.0 | 37 | His points, threes, FT% and steals fit any build, but a projected 15th to 19th finish puts him above the 25 to 75 core range. |
| [Tyrese Haliburton](#player/215) | IND | G | 10 | 49.8 | 14 | 39.4 | not drafted | His elite assists are a stable category, but the torn Achilles, early load management and a 3-4-3 playoff schedule make him a risk for a safety-first build. |
| [Jamal Murray](#player/400) | DEN | G | 17 | 37.0 | 22 | 25.7 | 27 | Points, assists, FT% and threes with no weak spot make him safe, but as a round 2 player he sits above the balanced range unless he falls to the experts' range. |

### 20 to 25 USD: core anchors

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Lauri Markkanen](#player/350) | UTA | F | 30 | 21.4 | 36 | 13.9 | 16 | His strong points, about 3 threes and elite FT% on volume are a stable scoring base, but check his health after only 42 games. |
| [Jalen Williams](#player/604) | OKC | F | 37 | 19.4 | 35 | 19.4 | 35 | Big assists and steals for a forward give him a rare category mix, and the market has dropped him into the core range. |
| [Trey Murphy III](#player/398) | NOP | G,F | 28 | 21.3 | 47 | 10.3 | 20 | His points, threes, FT% on volume and steals have no weak spot, but his role next to a healthy Murray decides whether the points hold. |
| [Kawhi Leonard](#player/331) | TOR | G,F | 36 | 24.9 | 20 | 26.5 | 20 | Per game he gives top 10 points, FT%, FG% and steals, but his knee makes him a buy only at the low end of this range. |

### 10 to 20 USD: core depth

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Nickeil Alexander-Walker](#player/12) | ATL | G | 58 | 5.7 | 33 | 11.7 | 1 | About 19 points plus threes and FT% with no weak category make him a clear value target in the core range. |
| [Kyrie Irving](#player/259) | DAL | G | 41 | 12.7 | 50 | 11.6 | not drafted | He adds points, FT% and threes at a market cost below his round 3 grade, and Dallas has a 4-4-4 playoff schedule. |
| [OG Anunoby](#player/20) | NYK | F | 66 | 5.4 | 71 | 5.4 | 15 | His value comes from steals and threes, which are less stable, and the Knicks' weak playoff schedule makes him a trade chip. |
| [Paul George](#player/189) | BOS | F | 73 | 2.3 | 91 | 4.0 | 9 | Steals, threes and FT% with possible extra usage as Boston's number two option make him underpriced, but watch his back-to-back rest. |
| [Franz Wagner](#player/577) | ORL | F | 50 | 12.8 | 68 | 8.9 | 26 | Points, FT% and assists as a forward are stable categories that you get at a fair price, as long as he keeps the point guard role. |
| [De'Aaron Fox](#player/179) | SAS | G | 69 | 3.9 | 53 | 9.7 | 21 | His assists (5.6) and steals (1.4) give a guard base with no weak category, but check that his minutes stay near 31. |
| [Ryan Rollins](#player/488) | MIL | G | 60 | 2.1 | 104 | 2.7 | not drafted | Steals, assists and threes with no weak flag make him a bargain at market cost, as long as he keeps the starting job. |
| [Tyler Herro](#player/234) | MIL | G | 65 | 5.8 | 65 | 8.3 | 14 | He adds points, threes and FT% with no weak category, if he gets 34 to 35 minutes in a crowded guard group. |
| [Desmond Bane](#player/30) | ORL | G,F | 48 | 9.1 | 41 | 13.0 | 22 | His 90% FT%, threes and points fit any build as a mid-round piece, but only at the real market price and not at last season's cost. |
| [Onyeka Okongwu](#player/422) | ATL | C | 49 | 7.6 | 44 | 6.7 | 6 | A center who adds threes and steals without hurting any category, but check his Q status and minutes first. |

### 5 to 12 USD: upside pieces

| Player | Team | Pos | Yahoo rank | Yahoo cost | ESPN rank | ESPN cost | Our league 2025-26 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Dylan Harper](#player/222) | SAS | G | 85 | 4.8 | 99 | 5.0 | not drafted | Assists and FG% with upside to the top 60, if he stays a starter at 29 or more minutes. |
| [Jaden McDaniels](#player/370) | MIN | F | 82 | 2.0 | 81 | 3.5 | 1 | His steals, blocks and 50.9% FG fit any build, but those categories swing more than points or assists, and Minnesota has a two-game semifinal week. |
| [Zach LaVine](#player/328) | SAC | G,F | 107 | 1.8 | 159 | 1.5 | 12 | A scorer with threes, points and good percentages whose draft position is rising, but check his minutes and any trade or buyout news. |
| [Norman Powell](#player/459) | CHI | G,F | 89 | 2.3 | 67 | 4.8 | 8 | 22.3 points and 2.9 threes as Chicago's likely top scorer, but a trade to a contender would cut his value before our playoffs. |
| [Cedric Coward](#player/120) | MEM | G,F | 77 | 3.0 | 127 | 1.4 | not drafted | A balanced wing with a 4-4-4 playoff schedule, though his low steals do little for steals-focused teams. |
